Just to go with @elarlang style guide and make it a bit more concise focusing on the positive defense strategy:

_Verify that XPath injection is not possible. Defense strategies include the use of XML libraries that support query parameterization or precompiled queries to separate logic from input. If parameterization is unavailable (e.g., in JavaScript's document.evaluate()), validate input and escape special characters according to XPath syntax._

Just to go with @elarlang style guide and make it a bit more concise focusing on the positive defense strategy, I would suggest:

_Verify that XPath injection is not possible. Defense strategies include the use of XML libraries that support query parameterization or precompiled queries to separate logic from input. If parameterization is unavailable (e.g., in JavaScript's document.evaluate()), validate input and escape special characters according to XPath syntax._

The requirement must explicitly say: “**Untrusted data is never directly concatenated into XPath queries.**”

I would suggest please replace this “**Verify that the application is protected against XPath injection attacks by** …” with specific, testable controls.
